clue.text: Supporters of solid fuel

parts.note: reads like backers of coal policy, but means metal stands holding logs in a fireplace

explanation.definitionFit: Andirons in a hearth hold up the burning logs.

clue.text: Respecting free and unconstrained polls

parts.note: re means concerning or respecting

indicators.note: unconstrained means set loose, so these letters are free to be rearranged

explanation.surface: With regard to free and open ballots.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda are public votes on a single question, the Latin plural form.

clue.text: Old Greek offering tip-top accommodation

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek offers the best rooms in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic means of ancient Athens; an attic is the room at the very top of a house.

clue.text: Belligerent Roman poet

explanation.surface: A warlike Roman versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Martial means warlike; Martial was a Latin poet famous for epigrams.

clue.text: A god's head set within a circle

indicators.note: set within means one piece is placed inside the letters that surround it

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O
poll is an old word for the head, as in a poll tax counted per head

explanation.surface: A deity's head is placed inside a ring, like a halo on an icon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set within' puts POLL between A and O, the circle; the second 'a' is only a link. 'god's' reads as 'god is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of the sun, music and prophecy is one of the Olympian gods.

clue.text: Professional investigator is an unhappy person

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a tester investigates by trying things out

explanation.surface: A professional detective is a miserable figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone demonstrating against something is showing discontent.

clue.text: Let the trainee rest

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on British learner-driver plates
ease is rest or relaxation

explanation.surface: Allow the apprentice a break.
explanation.walkthrough: British learner drivers display an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease property is to rent it out.

clue.text: Cook too much in connection with party

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: Overcooking food for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo food is to cook it for too long.

clue.text: The way the elderly may be put on

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
the aged are the elderly

explanation.surface: How old people might be dressed or treated.
explanation.definitionFit: A play that is staged is produced or put on for an audience.

clue.text: Judge it a major overhaul

parts.note: a referee judges a match, so judge gives REF

explanation.surface: A judge rules that something needs a thorough overhaul.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit is a thorough repair and re-equipping, especially of a ship.

clue.text: A relation possibly provides an explanation

indicators.note: possibly says these letters might be put into another order to make a different word

explanation.surface: A family member may be the reason that explains something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the nine letters of A RELATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reasoning or justification for something.

clue.text: City money invested in network making a comeback and leading.

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so these letters go inside another piece
making a comeback means the word for network is read backwards

parts.note: a grid is a network of lines or cables
EC is the postcode area for the City of London
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A financier's money is put into a reviving network that leads the market.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London, Britain's financial district, has the postcode EC; 'tin' as money is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Directing an effort is guiding or leading it.

clue.text: In some respects the men did better

indicators.note: in some respects suggests only part of the following words is used, the answer lies inside them

explanation.surface: The men performed better in certain ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In some respects' points to the letters inside thE MEN Did. 'better' is the verb, not the comparative.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to improve it by correcting errors.

clue.text: Popular among the top brass!

explanation.surface: A popular figure among the senior officers.
explanation.definitionFit: General means widespread or common to most people; a general is a senior army officer, one of the top brass.

clue.text: Augment control on violence

parts.note: a rein controls a horse, so to rein is to control
force is physical violence

explanation.surface: Increase restraints on violent behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce is to strengthen by adding more.

clue.text: Appear ambivalent, as the French said, with a woman

parts.note: dit is French for said, the past participle of dire
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Someone seems undecided, as the French put it, alongside a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to hesitate, unable to decide, which shows mixed feelings.

clue.text: Wild rose in a gentle arrangement

indicators.note: arrangement suggests these letters are ordered afresh, like flowers in a vase

explanation.surface: A wild rose in a soft floral display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' rearranges INAGENTLE; 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is sweetbriar, a European wild rose.

clue.text: Apprentices sent out with the horses

parts.note: a stud is a set of horses kept for breeding

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Trainees are dispatched to work with the horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent out' reads as dispatched, but 'out' is the anagram signal; 'the horses' is a breeding stud.
explanation.definitionFit: Students are learners, as apprentices are learners of a trade.

clue.text: Papers arranged in order to hide a bill — it's quite easy

indicators.note: to hide means something is concealed inside another piece, so letters go within

parts.note: a file is a set of papers kept in order
AC is short for account, which is a bill

explanation.surface: Filing papers neatly to conceal an invoice is no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' looks like an anagram signal but belongs to the description of papers kept in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Facile describes something achieved without effort, often too simply.

clue.text: Size of previous temporary home

parts.note: ex means former or previous
a tent is a temporary dwelling

explanation.surface: How big an old camping shelter was.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent is the scope, area or degree of something.

clue.text: Bird pictures framed by many to hire out

indicators.note: framed by means the pictures sit inside a border made by the other letters

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many
to let a property is to hire it out
pictures as a whole are art

explanation.surface: Paintings with a bird subject, hung in many frames, are rented out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' gives the Roman numeral for a thousand; the bird is also the footless one on coats of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A martlet is a swift or house martin, and a footless bird in heraldry.

clue.text: Electrical equipment agent perhaps filling in a medical man

indicators.note: filling in means one piece fills the space inside another

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An agent may be filling in for a doctor with electrical kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agent perhaps' reads as an example, but 'perhaps' is the anagram signal; MO, medical officer, is an army doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A magneto is a small generator producing current for ignition.

clue.text: Stick figure drawing

explanation.surface: A simple matchstick sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick figure' looks like one phrase; the split falls after 'Stick'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastel is a crayon stick of pigment, and a picture made with such crayons.

clue.text: Indifferent article written by retired clown

parts.note: a is the indefinite article in grammar

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or drawn back, so the word for clown is read backwards

parts.note: a fool is a clown or jester

explanation.surface: A disinterested piece is penned by a clown who has left the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests a clown who has stopped working; here it means drawn back, reading the word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof stays distant and uninvolved, cool towards others.

clue.text: He uses craft to make things easier

definitions.text: He uses craft to make things easier

parts.words: He uses craft to make things easier
parts.note: suggests a skilful helper; really someone lubricating machinery, and a tanker is also a craft carrying fuel

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lubricates machinery helps parts move smoothly.

clue.text: Get the din dealt with when put under some strain

indicators.note: dealt with suggests the letters are handled and sorted again, like cards being dealt

explanation.surface: Sort out a noise when you are under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tightened has been drawn taut, under tension.

clue.text: Twice a day the Chaplain called, and left a little — " (Wilde)

definitions.text: Twice a day the Chaplain called, and left a little

parts.words: Twice a day the Chaplain called, and left a little
parts.note: a line from Wilde's Ballad of Reading Gaol; the missing word is a religious pamphlet the prison chaplain leaves

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from Oscar Wilde's poem about prison life.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious leaflet is a short pamphlet left by a visiting clergyman.

clue.text: The play "Dream State" is receiving Spanish approbation

indicators.note: is receiving means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a trance is a dreamlike state
ole is the Spanish cry of approval heard at bullfights

explanation.surface: A drama titled Dream State gets cheers from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The play' looks like a stage work with 'Dream State' its title, but 'play' means slack in machinery.
explanation.definitionFit: In engineering, play is the allowed slack or variation in a fit, measured as a permitted margin.

clue.text: A story with point for a foreigner

parts.note: a story can be a lie, an untrue tale
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A tale with a moral for someone from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a person from another country, not a citizen.

clue.text: Drink out of the river — there's more of it!

indicators.note: out of here means the drink lies outside, surrounding the other letter

parts.note: lager is a drink, a light beer
R is an abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: Drinking beer from the river means there is plenty to go round.
explanation.definitionFit: Larger means bigger, describing something of which a greater amount exists.

clue.text: To discharge junior would be unavailing

parts.note: to boot someone out is to discharge them
less can mean younger or lesser, as in James the Less

explanation.surface: Sacking the junior employee would achieve nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Less' is an old title for the younger of two people with the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Bootless is an old word for useless, getting no result.
